_comment: WHAT IS ACTUALLY DEPLOYED, and where this hash CAME FROM.
PROVENANCE MATTERS MORE THAN THE VALUE. A hash copied off the chain and then compared back
to the chain proves nothing -- that is exactly the tautology verify_deployment.py was written
to replace (its predecessor pinned a constant lifted from the deployed program). Adversarial
review caught the first version of this file doing the same thing.
So the hash below is DERIVED, not observed: it is what commit a806f63's committed TEAL
artifact assembles to. That it also equals what the chain serves is the FINDING, not the
definition. `verify_deployment.py --against declared` re-derives it from that commit before
trusting it, so editing this value to match a chain would fail the provenance check rather
Do not edit a hash here to make a check pass. The correct response to a mismatch is to find

provenance.derived_by: assembling the committed TEAL artifact at the commit named in deployed_commit
provenance.method: algod POST /v2/teal/compile, then sha512_256 of the returned bytecode
provenance.NOT_derived_by: reading the program off the chain (that would make the declared check circular)

pending_redeploy.what_changed: register_cell gained: assert op.getbyte(committed_pubkey.native, 0) == 0x0A -- a Falcon-1024 (logn=10) public-key header check, at the only point a key enters state.
pending_redeploy.risk_while_pending: Contained. register_cell is admin-gated; PUBKEY_LEN is still enforced on the live app; falcon_verify rejects a malformed key at use time. The missing assert makes a bad key unusable rather than unregisterable, and admits no forgery. TestNet only, labelled UNAUDITED - not for MainNet value.
pending_redeploy.resolution: Redeploy from the committed artifact and update this file, or record a decision to keep 763809096 on a806f63 permanently.
